summary: Three families of tricks: (1) modular arithmetic — keep numbers small by taking %M after every +, −, *, with the ((x%M)+M)%M fix for negatives; (2) fast power — pow(a,n) mod M in O(log n) by halving; (3) Euclidean GCD — gcd(a,b) = gcd(b, a%b), base gcd(a,0)=a, runs in O(log min(a,b)). LCM falls out as a*(b/gcd). Almost every 'count pairs' problem on this day is solved by a frequency array of remainders.

thoughtProcess.title: 1. Stay inside the modulus.
thoughtProcess.body: Whenever the answer could exceed 2^31, switch to long and take %M after every arithmetic op. Two intermediates of size <1e9 each can be multiplied as long * long without overflow; cast first.

thoughtProcess.title: 2. Negative remainders are a real bug.
thoughtProcess.body: Java's % can return negative results (e.g. (-3) % 5 == -2). Always finish with ((x % M) + M) % M when subtraction or negative inputs are possible — Power Function does this explicitly.

thoughtProcess.title: 3. Fast power: halve, don't decrement.
thoughtProcess.body: pow(a,n) = pow(a,n/2)^2 (× a if n is odd). O(log n) instead of O(n). For n=1e9 the difference is TLE vs instant.

thoughtProcess.title: 4. GCD is the universal hammer.
thoughtProcess.body: Coprime tests, LCM, divisor-count counting, simplifying fractions, 'delete-one max GCD' — all use Euclidean gcd. Memorise: gcd(a,b) = b==0 ? a : gcd(b, a%b).

thoughtProcess.title: 5. Pair-sum-divisible: count remainders, not pairs.
thoughtProcess.body: For 'count i<j with (A[i]+A[j])%B==0': build freq[r] = count of A[i]%B==r, then result = C(freq[0],2) + Σ_{r=1..B/2-1} freq[r]*freq[B-r] + (B even ? C(freq[B/2],2) : 0). O(N+B) instead of O(N²).

thoughtProcess.title: 6. Mod-equality problems.
thoughtProcess.body: A%M == B%M ⇔ M divides (A−B). The maximum such M is |A−B|. One-line answer: return Math.abs(A − B). Don't iterate.

thoughtProcess.title: 7. Delete-one-element queries → prefix/suffix arrays.
thoughtProcess.body: When you need an aggregate (gcd, max, sum, min) of an array with element i removed, precompute prefix[i] = agg(A[0..i]) and suffix[i] = agg(A[i..N-1]). Removing i then costs O(1): combine prefix[i-1] with suffix[i+1].

thoughtProcess.title: Integer division truncates toward zero, not floor.
thoughtProcess.body: Java's / rounds toward zero, so (-7)/2 == -3, not -4. Combined with % keeping the dividend's sign, a == (a/b)*b + (a%b) always holds. When you need a true mathematical floor-divide for negatives (mapping coordinates to grid cells), use Math.floorDiv(a,b) and Math.floorMod(a,b).

thoughtProcess.title: Inclusion-Exclusion for 'divisible by any of a set'.
thoughtProcess.body: To count integers in [1..N] divisible by at least one of p1..pk: add single-divisor counts N/pi, subtract pairwise N/lcm(pi,pj), add triples, etc., alternating sign over the 2^k subsets. Each subset's divisor is the lcm of its members (compute via gcd, dividing first to avoid overflow).

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting non-negative adjustment in modular subtraction / negative base
commonMistakes.wrong: result = result % C;  // result of pow can be negative if A is negative
commonMistakes.why: Java's % preserves sign of dividend. (-3) % 5 = -2, not 3. Always normalise to [0, C).

commonMistakes.title: Overflow in (a * b) % m without casting
commonMistakes.wrong: int p = a * b % m;              // 1e5 * 1e5 = 1e10 overflows int
commonMistakes.why: int*int is safe only while each operand is <= ~46340 (product < 2^31). At a,b = 1e5 the product 1e10 already overflows int, so cast one operand to long before multiplying.

commonMistakes.title: Fast power decrement-by-one (TLE)
commonMistakes.wrong: long pow(long a, long n, long m) { if (n == 0) return 1; return (a * pow(a, n - 1, m)) % m; }
commonMistakes.why: Decrement is O(N). Halve-and-square is O(log N). Required for n ≤ 1e9.

commonMistakes.title: GCD base case at b==1 (wrong) instead of b==0
commonMistakes.wrong: int gcd(int a, int b) { if (b == 1) return 1; return gcd(b, a % b); }
commonMistakes.right: int gcd(int a, int b) { if (b == 0) return a; return gcd(b, a % b); }
commonMistakes.why: gcd(a,0) = a is the canonical base. gcd(5,1) = 1 by the recursion anyway, but b==1 cuts off chains like gcd(6,4) wrong.

commonMistakes.title: LCM via a*b/gcd overflowing
commonMistakes.right: long lcm = (long) a * (b / gcd(a, b));   // divide first to keep magnitude down
commonMistakes.why: a*b can overflow even when LCM itself fits. Divide-then-multiply order avoids the blow-up.

commonMistakes.title: Pair-sum-divisible counted twice or missing the (0, B/2) buckets
commonMistakes.wrong: for each r: count += freq[r] * freq[B - r];   // double-counts and crashes on r=0
commonMistakes.why: Buckets 0 and B/2 (when B even) pair with themselves: use n*(n-1)/2, NOT n*n. Other buckets pair once, not twice — loop r=1..B/2-1.

commonMistakes.title: Delete-one GCD: recomputing per index
commonMistakes.wrong: for each i: g = 0; for j != i: g = gcd(g, A[j]); ans = max(ans, g);  // O(N²)
commonMistakes.right:
// O(N): build prefix & suffix gcd arrays once
int without_i = gcd(prefix[i-1], suffix[i+1]);  // edges handled separately
commonMistakes.why: N up to 1e5 means O(N²) = 1e10 ops → TLE. Prefix/suffix gives O(N).

commonMistakes.title: Sieve inner loop starts at 2*i or uses int for i*i
commonMistakes.why: Multiples below i*i were already crossed off by smaller primes, so start at i*i. i*i exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE only when N approaches 2^31 (~2.1e9); for N ~= 1e9, i <= ~31623 so i*i ~= 1e9 still fits int. The (long) cast is defensive near the 2^31 boundary.

commonMistakes.title: Building factorial/nCr in a raw long without modding each step
commonMistakes.wrong:
long fact = 1;
for (int k = 1; k <= n; k++) fact *= k;   // 21! overflows signed 64-bit
commonMistakes.why: 20! = 2.4e18 fits, but 21! overflows long. Take %MOD after every multiply and divide via modular inverse (Fermat: inv = pow(x, MOD-2, MOD)) — you cannot use / under a modulus.

commonMistakes.title: Using / and % to bucket negative values into a grid
commonMistakes.wrong: int cell = value / size;      // (-1)/10 == 0, collides with cell 0
commonMistakes.why: Java / truncates toward zero, so negatives round the wrong way and collide with the 0 bucket. Math.floorDiv / Math.floorMod give consistent, contiguous buckets across the sign boundary.

keyPatterns.name: Fast Power (binary exponentiation, mod)
keyPatterns.when: Compute a^n mod M with n up to 1e9; also for modular inverse via Fermat (a^(M-2) mod M when M prime).

keyPatterns.name: Euclidean GCD (and LCM)
keyPatterns.when: Any divisibility, coprime, reducing-fraction, ratio question.

keyPatterns.name: Remainder-frequency pair counting
keyPatterns.when: Count (i,j) such that (A[i] ⊕ A[j]) satisfies a divisibility condition — sum%B, diff%B, etc.

keyPatterns.name: Coprime divisor extraction
keyPatterns.when: Largest divisor of A that is coprime with B — keep dividing A by gcd(A,B) until gcd becomes 1.

keyPatterns.name: Frequency-array pairwise mod-sum
keyPatterns.when: Sum / count over all pairs (a,b) with a small value range (≤ 1000) — replace the outer N² loop with iteration over distinct values.

keyPatterns.name: Mod-equality shortcut: |A−B|
Prefix + Suffix aggregate (delete-one)
keyPatterns.when: Aggregate (gcd, max, sum, product, xor) of array with element i removed; ascend N=1e5.

keyPatterns.name: Sieve of Eratosthenes
keyPatterns.when: Precompute all primes <= N (or smallest-prime-factor) when N <= ~1e7. O(N log log N) time, O(N) space.

keyPatterns.name: Modular multiplication of two large longs (mulmod)
keyPatterns.when: Multiplying two values each near M ~1e18 so even (long)*(long) overflows 64-bit.

edgeCases: Power Function with B = 0 → answer is 1 % C (so answer is 0 when C == 1).
Power Function with A < 0 → normalise the final result with ((res % C) + C) % C.
GCD of (0, 0) is conventionally 0; gcd(a, 0) = a.
LCM overflow: use long and divide-then-multiply (a/gcd) * b.
Pair Sum divisible: B = 1 → every pair qualifies, freq[0] = N, answer = C(N,2) mod 1e9+7.
Coprime Divisor: gcd(A,B) already 1 → return A as-is on the first iteration.
Divisor Game with B*C overflow: compute lcm as B * (C / gcd(B,C)) and use long.
Mod Sum: a == b contributes 0 to a%b; the outer loop running b from 1 and inner a from 1..b-1 skips it naturally.
A, B and Modulo with A == B → return 0 (still a valid M in the contract, though usually trivially handled).
Delete one with N == 2 → answer is max(A[0], A[1]) (deleting the other leaves a single element).
Sieve: allocate size N+1 and remember indices 0 and 1 are NOT prime; the outer loop only needs to run while i*i <= N.
nCr where r > n -> 0; r == 0 or r == n -> 1; guard before touching the factorial arrays.
Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) returns Integer.MIN_VALUE (still negative) — |A-B| can overflow int when values span the full range; use long.
Inclusion-exclusion: an empty subset contributes N (everything), and a subset's lcm can overflow — short-circuit when a partial lcm already exceeds N since N/lcm becomes 0.
Modular inverse via Fermat requires MOD prime and the value not a multiple of MOD; inverse of 0 is undefined.
